forces.label: Structure
forces.text: The National Armed Forces (NBS) consist of the Regular Forces, the National Guard (Zemessardze) and the Reserve. Chief of Defence: Major General Kaspars Pudāns.

forces.label: Peacetime strength (NATO count)
forces.text: NATO lists 8,200 military personnel for 2025 (estimate) and 8,300 for 2026 (estimate); the figure excludes trained reserves.

forces.label: Force target 2025-2036
forces.text: Development plan target: 61,000 soldiers, of which 31,000 peacetime (8,000 professional, 12,000 National Guard, 4,000 National Defence Service, 7,000 high-readiness reserve) plus 30,000 general reserve. This is a target, not current strength. The National Guard has four brigades: 1st Riga, 2nd Vidzeme, 3rd Latgale, 4th Kurzeme.

forces.label: National Guard (Zemessardze)
forces.text: The National Guard numbered about 10,000 guards in March 2025.

forces.label: Conscription
forces.text: National Defence Service (VAD): male citizens born after 1 January 2004 can be drafted; women and men aged 18-27 may volunteer. Service is 11 months in the regular forces or National Guard, or 5 years part-time in the National Guard, or a 5-year reserve officer programme.

forces.label: Latest conscript intake
forces.text: 1,277 people began National Defence Service on 17 July 2026, 1,225 of them in the 11-month programme; 647 joined the Land Forces Mechanised Infantry Brigade.

forces.label: Infantry fighting vehicles
forces.text: 84 ASCOD (Hunter) infantry fighting vehicles from GDELS-Santa Bárbara Sistemas, delivered in batches between the second half of 2026 and 2029.

forces.label: Armoured personnel carriers
forces.text: Patria 6x6 carriers in service since October 2021 and assembled in Valmiera since 2024; a full-cycle maintenance contract was signed on 11 March 2026. CVR(T) tracked vehicles equip the Mechanised Infantry Brigade.

forces.label: Air defence
forces.text: IRIS-T medium-range air defence system: first deliveries scheduled for 2026. RBS 70 NG short-range systems are to be procured in the coming years.

forces.label: Long-range fires
forces.text: HIMARS and ATACMS agreed with the US in 2023, to be delivered between 2027 and 2029. M109 self-propelled howitzers are being modernised.

forces.label: Artillery
forces.text: On 30 September 2026 the Ministry of Defence, the government of Slovakia and Tatra Defence Systems signed a trilateral agreement for 155 mm Morana artillery systems.

forces.label: Coastal defence
forces.text: Latvia is acquiring close- and far-range anti-ship missiles (Naval Strike Missile); the MoD page gives no delivery date.

forces.label: Helicopters
forces.text: Three UH-60M Black Hawk helicopters in service; the fourth is due in 2026.

forces.label: Allied forces: NATO Multinational Brigade Latvia
forces.text: Canada-led brigade of 14 nations: Albania, Canada, Czechia, Denmark, Iceland, Italy, Latvia, Montenegro, North Macedonia, Poland, Slovakia, Slovenia, Spain, Sweden. Command passed to Col. Dave Brassard on 10 June 2026 at Ādaži Military Base, in a ceremony presided over by the commander of Multinational Division North.

forces.label: Allied forces: Canada
forces.text: About 2,000 Canadian Armed Forces members are in Latvia under Operation REASSURANCE, which was extended through 2031 in July 2026. Canada will join Latvia and Denmark as the third framework nation of Multinational Division North.

forces.label: Peacetime strength (NATO count)
forces.text: NATO lists 19,000 military personnel for 2025 (estimate) and 20,200 for 2026 (estimate); the figure excludes trained reserves.

forces.label: Force target 2030
forces.text: Ministry plan of September 2024: professional soldiers to rise from 13,500 (2024) to 15,500 by 2030 and the active reserve to 50,000. The national division with assigned units is planned at about 17,500 soldiers and is expected to reach full operational capability by 2030.

forces.label: Conscription
forces.text: Men aged 18-22 are drafted after completing school. Service lasts nine months, with three- and six-month options introduced in 2026. About 5,000 conscripts are expected in 2026.

forces.label: Riflemen's Union
forces.text: Voluntary paramilitary civic organisation with about 18,000 members and a goal of 50,000 by 2035; it received EUR 24.2 million from the MoD for 2026.

forces.label: Tanks
forces.text: 44 Leopard 2A8 tanks ordered, enough for one battalion; 38 will be assembled at a plant in Kaunas whose construction began on 1 October 2026, with the first locally assembled tank expected at the end of 2028.

forces.label: Infantry fighting vehicles
forces.text: 100 CV90 MkIV vehicles: implementation agreement signed with five other NATO nations in June 2026, with Sweden negotiating for the group; first vehicles expected from 2028.

forces.label: Long-range fires
forces.text: Eight HIMARS launchers ordered in 2022 (USD 495 million) and a second battery added in April 2026 (USD 280 million). The military chief said on 10 September 2026 that US deliveries are behind schedule.

forces.label: Air defence and artillery
forces.text: About EUR 100 million is allocated in 2026 for a fourth NASAMS medium-range air defence system. 30 more CAESAR howitzers were ordered, bringing the total to 48.

forces.label: Allied forces: German brigade
forces.text: Panzerbrigade 45: two German combat battalions joined in late January 2026 and the Multinational Battlegroup Lithuania (about 1,700 soldiers) on 4 February 2026, giving the brigade three combat units. It is to be fully operational with more than 5,000 soldiers before 2028 and will move into a new barracks at Rūdninkai.

forces.label: Allied forces: NATO battlegroup
forces.text: Framework nation Germany; contributing nations Belgium, Czechia, Luxembourg, the Netherlands and Norway (as of June 2026).

forces.label: Baltic Air Policing, Šiauliai
forces.text: Italy took over on 31 July 2026 with four Eurofighter Typhoons, relieving a French detachment (four Rafale) and a Romanian detachment (six F-16).

forces.label: Wartime structure
forces.text: More than 43,000 positions: 4,200 filled by active-duty members of the Defence Forces and Defence League in permanent readiness, 38,800 by reservists. A supplementary reserve of 4,000 exists, about 40,000 further trained reservists are unassigned, and about 230,000 people are in the mobilisation register.

forces.label: Peacetime strength (NATO count)
forces.text: NATO lists 7,800 military personnel for 2025 (estimate) and 5,100 for 2026 (estimate); the fall is as published and unexplained in the tables.

forces.label: Conscription
forces.text: Compulsory for physically and mentally healthy male citizens; women may volunteer. Conscript service lasts 11 months in 2026.

forces.label: Estonian Division
forces.text: Largest land unit: 1st Infantry Brigade, 2nd Infantry Brigade, Headquarters and Signal Battalion, ISTAR Battalion, Artillery Regiment, Logistics Battalion, Engineer Battalion. It is subordinated to Multinational Corps Northeast in the NATO chain of command.

forces.label: Defence League (Kaitseliit)
forces.text: About 18,000 members; more than 30,000 volunteers including the women's and youth organisations.

forces.label: Long-range fires
forces.text: Six HIMARS launchers were handed over to the Defence Forces on 30 April 2025 at Ämari Air Base; the contract was signed in December 2022.

forces.label: Air defence
forces.text: The Air Defence Wing received its first IRIS-T SLM medium-range systems on 22 June 2026 at Ämari Air Base.

forces.label: Budget priorities
forces.text: EUR 3.4 billion is allocated to ammunition for 2025-2029; procurement reaches EUR 1.27 billion in 2026; defence spending stays at no less than 5% of GDP in 2027-2029.

forces.label: Allied forces: UK-led battlegroup
forces.text: Stationed at Tapa since 2017 and integrated into the 1st Infantry Brigade; the United Kingdom is framework nation and France contributes a company-sized unit. The UK 4th Brigade has been held at high readiness in the UK to reinforce Estonia since summer 2025.

forces.label: Allied forces: United States
forces.text: US soldiers serve in Estonia on a rotational basis under a bilateral agreement, at Tapa and at Reedo near Võru.

forces.label: Baltic air defence mission, Ämari
forces.text: Turkish Air Force F-16s hold the rotation from 1 August to 30 November 2026; Spanish Air Force F-18s were added from 8 September to early October 2026.
